---

**This is the stage that costs money.** It ends by writing raw, unframed art to
`tarot/derived-art/`, one file per card, named by slot: `00_the-fool.png`, `16_the-tower.png`.
Stage 2 picks that folder up.

## Why this is split from the assembly

Generation is slow and paid; borders and lettering are instant and free. Keeping them in one
graph means every experiment with a keyline sits downstream of 78 API calls. Cut here and a
border is a stage-2 problem you can chew on all evening at no cost.

The result cache already makes a re-queue cheap, but only while the request is byte-identical
— change one word of the style block and it is gone. **A file on disk is not.**

## The handoff

Two things cross the boundary, and both are files:

- **The art**, named `{index:02d}_{label}` so stage 2's Slot Loader maps it straight back onto
  the right positions.
- **The deck definition**, written to `tarot/deck.json` by `save_definition_to`. Stage 2 loads
  that same file rather than re-declaring the deck, so the two stages cannot drift apart on
  names, order or scope. If you rename a card here, stage 2 letters the new name.

`save_sidecar_json` is on, so each card lands beside a JSON of the prompt that made it.

## Before you run

`scope` is on **proof set** — twelve cards that exercise every scoping dimension. Read the
Resolve report, and only then switch to `full deck`.
